PRIMARY EVIDENCE FOR DECISION D-008
===================================
PyTorch installs correctly on the Windows host but cannot be imported. The cause is a host
security policy, not a broken installation.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 -- install succeeds
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements-in.txt
Looking in indexes: https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu, https://pypi.org/simple
  Downloading .../cpu/torch-2.14.0%2Bcpu-cp312-cp312-win_amd64.whl (124.0 MB)
Successfully installed ... numpy-2.5.3 ... torch-2.14.0+cpu ...

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 2 -- numpy imports fine (its binaries are signed / judged reputable)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ .venv\Scripts\python.exe -c "import numpy;print('numpy ok',numpy.__version__)"
numpy ok 2.5.3

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 3 -- torch does not
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ .venv\Scripts\python.exe -c "import torch;print(torch.__version__)"
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
  File "C:\Users\titus\Music\projects\.venv\Lib\site-packages\torch\__init__.py", line 309, in <module>
    _load_dll_libraries()
  File "C:\Users\titus\Music\projects\.venv\Lib\site-packages\torch\__init__.py", line 292, in _load_dll_libraries
    raise err
OSError: [WinError 4551] An Application Control policy has blocked this file.
Error loading "C:\Users\titus\Music\projects\.venv\Lib\site-packages\torch\lib\shm.dll"
or one of its dependencies.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 4 -- root cause: Smart App Control is ON and enforcing
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\CI\Policy'
EmodePolicyRequired                   : 0
SkuPolicyRequired                     : 0
VerifiedAndReputablePolicyState       : 1     <-- 1 = Smart App Control ENABLED / enforcing
SAC_EnforcementReason                 : 3
SAC_PreviousState                     : 0
VerifiedAndReputableIgnoreAutoOptOut  : 1

Interpretation: Smart App Control refuses to load binaries it does not judge
verified-and-reputable. PyTorch's Windows wheels ship unsigned DLLs (torch\lib\shm.dll among
them), so the loader is blocked. Reinstalling, changing wheel versions, or using conda does not
change this -- the policy is about code signing, not about the package.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 5 -- the escape route, verified
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Smart App Control governs Windows PE binaries. Linux ELF binaries executing inside the WSL2 VM
are outside its scope, and Docker Desktop is already installed and running.

$ docker run --rm -v <repo>:/work -w /work ml-labs:cpu python -c "import torch;print(...)"
TORCH_OK 2.14.0+cpu

Host security posture unchanged. Smart App Control remains enabled.
